newsitem.title: USA: NBA-ILL JORDAN LEADS BULLS WITHIN ONE WIN OF FIFTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NBA-ILL JORDAN LEADS BULLS WITHIN ONE WIN OF FIFTH TITLE.

text.p: Michael Jordan was sick as a dog the night before, but courageously carried the Chicago Bulls to a 90-87 victory over the Utah Jazz Wednesday that put the defending champions one win away from their fifth NBA title in seven years.
Jordan, playing all but four minutes of the game, scored 38 points on 13-for-27 shooting from the floor and 10-for-12 from the line, and hit a key 3-pointer with 25 seconds to go.
"I was really tired, I was very weak," Jordan said. "At halftime I told Phil (coach Phil Jackson) to use me in spurts, but somehow I found the energy and just stayed strong. I wanted it really bad."

Jordan, who skipped the game day practice after vomiting all night, added seven rebounds and five assists as the best-of-seven Finals head back to Chicago for Game 6 on Friday, and if necessary, Game 7 on Sunday.
"It was a hell of an effort just for him to come out and play in this game. The effort that he gave us was just unbelievable," said Scottie Pippen, who was second high on the Bulls with 17 points.'
"He felt like he was going to faint. I guess he was pretty dehyrdrated and just tired, but he gutted it out," Pippen said of Jordan. "We owe this win to him. He did everything he could to carry us."
The Jazz, seeking their first championship in their first Finals, were led by Karl Malone's 19 points and six assists.
Centre Greg Ostertag came up big with 13 points and 15 rebounds and John Stockton also scored 13 for Utah.
The Jazz led by as many as 16 points and were ahead for the majority of the game. But the Bulls caught Utah at 85-85 when Jordan made 1-of-2 free throws with 46.5 left.
Chicago's Toni Kukoc tipped out the miss on Jordan's second free throw to keep possession and Jordan hit a 3-pointer to make it 88-85.
An Ostertag shot down low cut the lead to 88-86, but with the Jazz pressing fullcourt, the Bulls got the ball to Luc Longley under the basket for a jam and a 90-87 lead with six seconds to go.
Jeff Hornacek missed a potentially game-tying 3-pointer and Stockton made 1-of-2 free throws for the final score.
